title: Do not silently swallow exceptions
why: A handler that only passes or continues hides failures and lets execution proceed without recovery evidence.
suggestion: Handle the expected failure, log or translate it at a boundary, or document an explicit suppression.
limitations: Only bare, Exception, and BaseException handlers whose direct statements are pass or continue are reported.
Specific exception handlers are excluded because they commonly encode intentional fallback control flow.
A swallowed broad handler replaces bare-except and broad-except findings at the same location.
